LARRY THOMPSON: “THE SANITY MAN”

Sanity Isn’t More Right or More Left. It’s Forward.

I am running for United States Congress because I believe America is exhausted by political extremes, endless fighting, and leaders who seem more interested in themselves and their political party winning arguments, rather than solving our problems.

So, from today through Election [NAME], my campaign will stand for one simple idea:

SANITY.

Sanity means seeing reality clearly, rejecting the extremes of both sides, and choosing practical, common sense, solutions that actually improve people’s lives.

You don’t have to change your party to vote for Sanity in this election.

Sanity has no party. It belongs to everyone.

Sanity is on the ballot.

Sanity means:

[NAME] over politics.
Common sense over ideology.
Results over seniority.
Courage over blind party loyalty.
Accountability with compassion.
Innovation with responsibility.
The future instead of the status quo.

I am not running to tell Democrats they have to become Republicans.

I am not running to tell Republicans they have to abandon their principles.

And I am not asking Independents to choose a political tribe.

I am only asking everyone to look at the problems in front of us and ask one question:

Who makes more sense?

Affordability is not a Republican problem or a Democratic problem.

Neither are wildfire prevention, insurance, homelessness, crime, traffic, rebuilding the Pacific Palisades and Malibu, cleaning up Santa Susana, restoring Hollywood jobs, preparing our children for the AI economy, making government work better, or just having someone tell us the truth.

These are everyone’s problems.

And solving them will require something Washington has been missing for far too long:

SANITY.

What Sanity Means

Sanity means reducing unnecessary costs, controlling government spending, supporting small businesses, creating better-paying jobs, and building an economy in which families can once again believe that tomorrow will be better than today.

Sanity means supporting law enforcement, demanding accountability, protecting civil liberties, and making every neighborhood safe.

Sanity means compassion for people experiencing homelessness—but compassion must include shelter, treatment, mental-health services, personal responsibility, and measurable results. Endless spending without meaningful improvement is not compassion. It is government failure.

Sanity means preventing wildfires before they destroy our communities—clearing dangerous vegetation, hardening neighborhoods, improving evacuation systems, strengthening emergency response, and rebuilding without years of bureaucratic delay.

Sanity means securing our borders while respecting due process. A sane country can protect its laws, its security, its workers, and its humanity at the same time.

Sanity means protecting Social Security, Medicare, veterans, national defense, and essential public services while confronting waste, irresponsible borrowing, and a federal debt that we cannot simply leave to our children. A sane government cannot promise everything, borrow forever, and pretend the bill will never arrive.

Sanity does not mean fearing artificial intelligence or blindly surrendering to it. It means leading the AI revolution, protecting privacy and human creativity, establishing human accountability, preparing workers for changing industries, and ensuring that the technologies of the future serve people—not the other way around.

California invented the modern entertainment industry. It is not sane to stand by while film, television, jobs, productions, and creative talent leave our state for other parts of the country and the world. We must make California competitive again and bring Hollywood employment home.

Accepting permanent gridlock on the 405 is not a transportation policy.

Sanity means pursuing a modern, high-speed transit connection between the San Fernando Valley and the Westside—bold enough to change people’s lives and practical enough to work.

It is not sane to allow generations of families near the Santa Susana Field Laboratory to continue waiting for a complete and safe cleanup. Government must establish deadlines, enforce accountability, protect the surrounding communities, and finish the job.

Sanity also means reforming Congress itself.

Members of Congress should read legislation before voting on it, explain their decisions to the people they represent, identify unintended consequences, and measure whether government programs actually produce the results they promised.

Leading the world in artificial intelligence is bold—but rational if we protect privacy, jobs, creators, and human accountability.

Reforming government is bold—but rational if it produces faster, smarter, more accountable public service.

Preparing California for the next generation of industries is bold—but rational if we want our children competing in tomorrow’s industries instead of yesterday’s jobs.

I believe politics should be about solving problems—not protecting political careers.

I believe we can disagree without hating one another.

I believe compassion and accountability can coexist.

I believe innovation and responsibility can coexist.

The future and AI are going to happen either WITH US or TO US. I’d rather California lead it than watch someone else build it.

It is not sane when hardworking people cannot afford to live in the communities where they work.

And I believe California’s 32nd Congressional District should be represented by someone thinking about the next 30 years—not relying on the last 30.

That is what “The Sanity Man” means.

It is more than a slogan.

It is the philosophy of this campaign.

And, I hope, the beginning of something much bigger.

THE NEXT 30 YEARS

[NAME] Over Politics.

I am not asking you to change your party.

I am asking you to judge the two candidates, the person, their ideas, their character, and their results.

You can remain a Democrat, Republican, or Independent and still vote for Sanity.

This election does not have to be another predictable battle between Democrats and Republicans.

It can be a choice between political performance and practical leadership.

Between accepting yesterday’s failures and building tomorrow’s opportunities.

You don't have to change your party.

You don't have to change your values.

You don't have to change who you are.

I am simply asking you to look at the problems in front of us and ask:

Who makes more sense?

Affordability is not Republican or Democratic.

Neither are insurance, wildfire prevention, rebuilding the Pacific Palisades, homelessness, public safety, traffic, bringing film and television jobs back to California, cleaning up Santa Susana, preparing our children for the AI economy, or making government work better.

These are everyone’s problems.

And they require practical solutions here at home—not another generation of political warfare in Washington.

Some of those solutions may be bold.

Good.

A high-speed monorail to help relieve gridlock along the 405 is bold—but rational if it works.

Making America the world leader in artificial intelligence is bold—but rational if we also protect privacy, creators, jobs, due process, and human accountability.

Bringing Hollywood production back to California is ambitious—but rational when one of our signature industries is losing thousands of jobs.

Reforming government is bold—but rational if government becomes faster, smarter, more efficient, and more accountable.

Preparing our children for industries and jobs that barely existed a decade ago is bold—but rational if we want them competing for tomorrow's opportunities instead of yesterday's jobs.

The next 30 years will bring changes most of us can barely imagine.

We can fear those changes.

We can ignore them.

Or we can lead them.

I choose to lead.

I believe California should lead the future rather than chase it.

I believe Congress needs leaders who are building the future—not “outlawing” or legislating the past.

I believe politics should be about solving problems—not protecting political careers.

I believe we can disagree without hating one another.

I believe compassion and accountability can coexist.

I believe innovation and responsibility can coexist.

I believe government can be both humane and efficient.

And I believe we can build a future that is safer, more affordable, more prosperous, more innovative—and more hopeful than the world we see around us today.

That is the choice I want this campaign to represent.

Not Republican versus Democrat.

Not Left versus Right.

But:

Past versus Future.

Noise versus Results.

Ideology versus Common Sense.

Politics versus [NAME].

And ultimately:

CHAOS VERSUS SANITY.

That is what The Sanity Man means.

It is not just a nickname.

It is not just a campaign slogan.

It is a governing philosophy.

See reality as it is.

Listen to people instead of political parties.

Use common sense.

Embrace good ideas wherever they come from.

Demand accountability.

Solve problems.

Prepare for what comes next.

And never be afraid to think big when thinking big actually makes sense.

Washington has enough people fighting yesterday's political battles.

I am running to help build tomorrow.

California's 32nd District is uniquely positioned to LEAD OUR FUTURE.

Our region is home to world-class entrepreneurs, engineers, universities, aerospace companies, creative professionals, and technology innovators. We should become America's premier district for AI, entertainment technology, medical innovation, aerospace, robotics, and digital entrepreneurship.

These industries create high-paying jobs, attract investment, strengthen national security, and ensure the next generation builds the future here rather than somewhere else.

I don't want our children competing for yesterday's jobs. I want them creating tomorrow's industries.

America's next great chapter will not be written by politicians who merely preserve the status quo. It will be written by innovators, entrepreneurs, teachers, scientists, engineers, first responders, veterans, small-business owners, and citizens willing to imagine what our country can become.

Throughout my legal and entertainment career, I've had the privilege of working in an industry built on creativity, innovation, and bold ideas. I've learned that success comes not from fearing change, but from leading it responsibly.

This campaign isn't about reliving the debates of the past or simply, but proudly, celebrating America’s 250th Anniversary, but about preparing America for the year 2050 and beyond.

I envision a nation where government is more efficient, our economy is driven by innovation, our children are equipped for the jobs of tomorrow, our borders are secure, our communities are safe, our veterans receive the care they deserve, Social Security and Medicare are protected, and our national debt is reduced through greater fiscal responsibility and more effective government—not by asking hardworking Americans to pay even higher taxes.

I don't believe Washington needs more career politicians.

I believe Washington needs new and better builders of the future.

History remembers the generations that built the future, not those that feared it. The next 30 years begin now. Let's make sure they become California's— and America's—greatest years of innovation, opportunity, and leadership.

Why I Am Running

I have spent my life bringing strong personalities together, negotiating difficult agreements, managing budgets, anticipating change, solving problems, and helping creative people turn ambitious ideas into reality. I have: 
• managed the careers of more than 250 stars
• produced 21 movies for television 
• produced five motion pictures
• produced television series and specials
• worked as a Broadway producer
• worked as an Entertainment lawyer
• worked as a talent manager
• authored a bestselling self-help book
• received the Talent Managers Lifetime Achievement Award
• been inducted into the Personal Manager's Hall of Fame
• been Knighted in Italy as a "Patron of the Arts and Protector of the Most Needy"
I want to bring my experience to politics and represent real people with their real problems.

THE NEXT 30 YEARS BEGIN NOW.

Less Noise. More Sanity.

[NAME] Over Politics.

Not Left. Not Right. Forward.

Sanity Is on the Ballot.

Vote Sanity. Vote [NAME], "The Sanity Man," for Congress.

Congress should not be a permanent stage for outrage, division, and political performance.

It should be a place where serious people solve serious problems.

My Sanity Pledge

As your representative:

1. I will tell voters the truth, even when it is inconvenient.
2. I will explain my votes and decisions.
3. I will work with anyone whose ideas benefit our district and our country.
4. I will demand measurable results from government spending.
5. I will prepare California for the next generation, not merely the next election.
6. I will represent my constituents first, not my party.

Imagine the welcomed irony of California’s CA-32, of all places, sending “The Sanity Man” from Southern California to Congress.

A BILL 

To improve access to evidence-based mental health services, strengthen family and community resilience, support veterans and first responders, address root causes of mental health challenges, and promote faith-based and local solutions, without creating new expansive federal bureaucracies or unfunded mandates.

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

(a) Short Title.  This Act may be cited as the “Mental Health Access and Family Resilience Act” or “MHARA.”

(b) Table of Contents. 

Sec. 1. Short title; table of contents.
Sec. 2. Findings and purpose.
Sec. 3. Definitions.
Sec. 4. Expanding access to mental health services.
Sec. 5. Veterans and first responders’ mental health support.
Sec. 6. Family resilience and prevention.
Sec. 7. Workforce development and provider training.
Sec. 8. Suicide prevention and crisis intervention.
Sec. 9. Integration with substance abuse prevention and treatment.

Sec. 11. Youth and school-based family partnerships.
Sec. 12. Research, innovation, and data collection.
Sec. 13. Accountability, oversight, and reporting.
Sec. 14. Authorization of appropriations.
Sec. 15. Effective date; sunset provision.

SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE.

Congress finds the following:

(1) [NAME] families, faith communities, and personal responsibility form the foundation of mental resilience, as evidenced by reduced rates of depression, substance abuse, and suicide in stable family structures.

(2) Veterans, first responders, and residents in underserved communities, including Bexar County and Texas’s 20th Congressional District, face disproportionate mental health challenges, including PTSD, trauma from service, and economic stressors.

(3) Root causes such as family breakdown, substance abuse, gang violence, and limited community-based support must be addressed alongside clinical services.

(4) Expanding access to telehealth, peer support, and faith-informed counseling, while incentivizing private and local innovation, provides cost-effective, dignity-affirming care.

(5) Substance use disorders and mental health conditions frequently co-occur, exacerbating cycles of family breakdown, unemployment, and instability, particularly among veterans and in high-poverty areas like parts of Bexar County.

(6) Homelessness is often intertwined with untreated mental illness and substance abuse; stable housing paired with voluntary, family-centered treatment and personal accountability promotes long-term recovery and resilience.

The purpose of this Act is to enhance mental health access, build family resilience, and empower communities and veterans through targeted, accountable measures.

SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS.

(1) Family Resilience Programs: Evidence-based initiatives that strengthen marriage, parenting, and intergenerational support networks.

(2) Faith-Based Providers: Nonprofit organizations operating consistently with sincerely held religious beliefs that deliver mental health support.

(3) Veterans: Individuals who served in the uniformed services, as defined in section 101 of title 38, United States Code.

(4) Telehealth: Includes audio-visual and audio-only services compliant with HIPAA.

SECTION 4. EXPANDING ACCESS TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES.

(a) Medicaid and CHIP Flexibility. States may use Medicaid and Children’s Health Insurance Program funds for intensive community-based mental health services, including peer support and family counseling, with emphasis on veterans and children.

(b) Telehealth Expansion. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall extend and simplify telehealth coverage for mental health services in rural and underserved areas, including Texas districts, with parity for audio-only when clinically appropriate.

(c) Block Grants for Community Providers. Authorizes $20 million annually (subject to appropriations) in competitive grants to States and localities for community mental health clinics, prioritizing partnerships with veterans’ organizations, faith-based groups, and family-focused nonprofits.

SECTION 5. VETERANS AND FIRST RESPONDERS’ MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT.

(a) VA Peer Support Enhancement. Directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to expand peer-to-peer counseling programs, including the “Be There” program and veteran-serving organizations.

(b) Caregiver Support. Provides grants for caregiver mental health training and respite services for families of veterans with service-connected conditions.

(c) Law Enforcement and First Responders. Authorizes grants for officer wellness, peer support, and stigma-reduction programs modeled on successful bipartisan initiatives.

SECTION 6. FAMILY RESILIENCE AND PREVENTION.

(a) Family Strengthening Grants. Establishes a grant program through the Department of Health and Human Services for evidence-based programs that promote marriage education, parenting skills, and family counseling, with priority for high-poverty areas like parts of San Antonio.

(b) School-Based Family Partnerships. Encourages (without mandates) local educational agencies to partner with community organizations for voluntary family resilience workshops.

(c) Root Cause Initiatives. Supports data-driven programs addressing substance abuse, gang intervention, and fatherhood initiatives as preventive mental health measures.

SECTION 7. WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDER TRAINING.

(a) Mental Health Workforce Grants. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall establish a competitive grant program to States and eligible entities (including community colleges, veterans’ organizations, and faith-based institutions) to recruit, train, and retain mental health professionals, with priority for providers serving rural and underserved areas, veterans, and families.

(b) Training Emphasis. Grants shall support evidence-based training in trauma-informed care, family systems approaches, peer support, and integration of faith-based counseling where appropriate and consistent with provider's mission.

(c) Loan Repayment Incentives. Authorizes expansion of existing loan repayment programs for mental health providers committing to service in high-need districts, including Bexar County, Texas.

SECTION 8. SUICIDE PREVENTION AND CRISIS INTERVENTION.

(a) 988 Lifeline Enhancement. Directs the Secretary to strengthen the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline with improved routing to local, community, and faith-based responders.

(b) Veterans Suicide Prevention. Expands VA programs modeled on successful peer and community initiatives, including outreach to veterans’ families.

(c) Community Crisis Response. Authorizes grants for local crisis stabilization units and mobile response teams that prioritize de-escalation, family involvement, and diversion from hospitalization or incarceration.

SECTION 9. INTEGRATION WITH SUBSTANCE ABUSE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT.

(a) Co-Occurring Disorders Coordination. The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in coordination with the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, shall improve integration of mental health and substance use disorder services through joint funding opportunities, shared screening protocols, and care coordination models that prioritize evidence-based treatment for co-occurring conditions.

(b) Prevention and [NAME] Intervention. Authorizes grants to States and localities for community-based programs targeting root causes, including opioid misuse, methamphetamine, fentanyl, and alcohol abuse, with emphasis on veteran-specific outreach, family involvement, peer recovery coaches, and faith-based recovery support networks.

(c) Treatment and Recovery Expansion. Supports expansion of residential and outpatient treatment programs, including family-centered recovery options and incentives for long-term sobriety through job training and mentorship tied to personal responsibility.

(d) Veterans Focus. Directs the VA to enhance programs addressing substance use alongside PTSD and other service-related conditions, building on successful peer support and community reintegration models.

(e) Accountability Measures. Programs funded under this section shall emphasize measurable outcomes such as reduced relapse rates, family reunification, and decreased justice system involvement, with preference for providers demonstrating cost-effectiveness and voluntary participation.

SECTION 10. ADDRESSING HOMELESSNESS AS A MENTAL HEALTH AND FAMILY STABILITY PRIORITY.

(a) Housing-First with Treatment Integration. Authorizes competitive grants to local governments, veterans’ organizations, faith-based nonprofits, and community providers for supportive housing programs that combine stable housing with voluntary mental health and substance abuse treatment, prioritizing veterans, families, and individuals with co-occurring disorders.

(b) Local Innovation and Accountability. Grants shall favor evidence-based approaches that encourage personal responsibility, family reunification where appropriate, and partnerships with job training and life-skills programs. Nothing in this section shall mandate Housing First models that de-emphasize treatment or enable ongoing substance abuse.

(c) Veterans and Family Emphasis. Expands eligibility and funding flexibility for VA and HUD programs serving homeless veterans with mental health needs, including caregiver support and transitional housing that strengthens family units. Prioritizes projects in high-need districts such as TX-20.

(d) Crisis Diversion and Prevention. Supports mobile outreach teams, crisis stabilization centers, and rapid rehousing initiatives that divert individuals from streets or emergency rooms into treatment and housing pathways, with strong coordination between mental health providers, law enforcement, and community organizations.

(e) Reporting and Safeguards. Recipients must report on outcomes including housing stability, treatment engagement, reduced recidivism to homelessness, and cost savings. Protects religious liberty for faith-based providers and prohibits the use of funds to promote or enable illegal drug use.

SECTION 11. YOUTH AND SCHOOL-BASED FAMILY PARTNERSHIPS.

(a) Voluntary Programs. Encourages local educational agencies to partner with families and community organizations for voluntary mental health education, resilience-building, and parental involvement workshops.

(b) Child and Adolescent Focus. Authorizes targeted grants for early intervention services emphasizing family stability, avoiding ideological approaches, and protecting parental rights.

(c) No Mandates. Nothing in this section shall be construed to impose new requirements on schools or infringe on local control or parental authority.

SECTION 12. RESEARCH, INNOVATION, AND DATA COLLECTION.

(a) Evidence-Based Research. Directs the National Institutes of Health, in coordination with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to prioritize research on family resilience factors, faith-informed interventions, and cost-effective community models.

(b) Outcome Metrics. Requires standardized data collection on program effectiveness, focusing on reduced suicide rates, hospitalizations, substance use, and improved family stability indicators.

(c) Innovation Grants. Establishes limited demonstration projects for novel local solutions, with rigorous evaluation and sunset after 3 years.

SECTION 13. ACCOUNTABILITY, OVERSIGHT, AND REPORTING.

(a) Reporting Requirements. The Secretary of HHS and the Secretary of VA shall submit annual reports to Congress on outcomes, including metrics on reduced hospitalizations, suicide rates, and family stability indicators.

(b) Sunset Provision. This Act shall expire after 5 years unless reauthorized, ensuring fiscal responsibility.

(c) No New Entitlements. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to create an individual entitlement to services.

SECTION 14. AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.

There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, with amounts allocated across sections subject to annual appropriations and oversight to ensure fiscal responsibility.

SECTION 15. EFFECTIVE DATE; SUNSET PROVISION.

(a) This Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment.
